re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1053
### Root Cause
- Review prompts had no evidence rule for external-spec claims, so legs asserted "the spec/reference says X" at 🚨 BLOCKING without reading the source (live: a false exemption-list claim held a validated PR hostage).
- Machine-side, `postPRReviewComments.js` relayed such findings verbatim into threads, census, and the verdict record — one uncited claim could arm rework.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js` (new, pure): detects external-spec claims, verifiable citations (`file:line` / doc URL), classifies effective severity — uncited spec claim → non-blocking; cited claims keep full BLOCKING force.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: `applySpecClaimDowngrades` sanitizes `pr_review.json` before any verdict/census/posting — rewrites 🚨→⚠ bodies with a "confirm against source" note, rebalances `issueCounts`, collapses `REQUEST_CHANGES`→`APPROVE` when no cited blocker remains.
- `instructions/pr_review/general_guidelines.md`: new "External-spec evidence rule (gh-1053)"; `review_verdict_rules.md`: matching anti-pattern.

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewSpecClaims.js` — 18 tests: uncited spec claim → non-blocking (AC2/AC3), cited claim stays BLOCKING (AC4), non-spec findings untouched, census/verdict rebalancing. PASSED.
- `test_postPRReviewComments.js` — 2 wiring tests for `applySpecClaimDowngrades`. PASSED (93/93 in suite).
- Full suite: 4333 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- Downgrade target is IMPORTANT (non-blocking), phrased as a confirm-against-source question per AC2; the note invites re-raising as BLOCKING with a citation.
- Review test suites loading `postPRReviewComments.js` gained the new require mapping in their harnesses.

# gh-1053: Review legs must not post BLOCKING findings built on unverifiable external-spec claims

## Description

## Problem

AI review legs post **BLOCKING review threads whose core claim is "the external spec/reference says X" — without reading that reference**. The claim is unfalsifiable inside the leg, and when it is wrong the machine treats the thread as real rework demand: rework arms, legs dispatch, a green PR is held hostage until a human disproves the claim.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, dmtools-dart PR #423)

Review leg posted a 🚨 BLOCKING thread claiming "the spec (ticket, Java `JsEnvPolicy`) exempts only `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT`". The claim was false — Java uses contains-based exemptions (`JsEnvPolicy.java:61-66`), and the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it. Cost: a rework arm on a validated PR, two leg dispatches, human intervention.

Note: the Java-parity specifics of that case live in the dmtools-dart project — THIS issue is only about the general discipline, which applies to every deployment of this pack.

## Root cause

The review prompt has no rule about evidence for external-spec claims. A model without access to the referenced source fills the gap with plausible-sounding "the spec says" assertions — at BLOCKING severity, which the SM machinery then treats as ground truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review agents never assert "spec/reference/tool X does/does not Y" as a BLOCKING finding unless the finding quotes the exact source (file:line / doc URL) the leg actually read during the run.
- [ ] A spec-claim finding without a verifiable citation is downgraded to a non-blocking question ("please confirm against <source>").
- [ ] Unit test: review output containing an external-spec claim without a citation is classified non-blocking.
- [ ] Verified findings with citations keep full BLOCKING force — this is not a strictness cut.

## Non-goals

- Project-specific reference setups (e.g. Java-source verification for the dmtools-dart port) — those belong to the consuming project.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39153304741) · started 18:15 · done 18:33 ✅

- [x] ▶ dev (fa-rework) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39155457257) · started 18:44 · done 18:47 🚫

`classifyFindingSeverity` (CC 23, fully covered → CRAP 23) exceeds the threshold on complexity alone: the ratchet only admits new functions with CRAP ≤ 8, so no coverage percentage can save a CC > 8 function. Please split it — e.g. extract per-comment resolution (`body`/`comment` + `readText`), per-comment demotion application, and census/verdict rebalancing into separate ≤ 8-CC helpers.

The test side needs slimming too: `loadWithFileMap` (CC 23.4) duplicates the entire require-map construction — extract a shared `requireMap()` helper used by both it and the existing loaders, and collapse the nested `file_read` factories (the CC 8.7 `file_read#10`) into one small resolver function reused at both call sites.

Note for verification: `nyc instrument` + `crap4js --baseline` reproduces the verdict locally (install `github:IstiN/crap4js#83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` + `nyc@17` as in `.github/workflows/quality.yml`).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: incidental spec mentions demote genuine BLOCKING bugs — verdict can collapse to APPROVE with a real defect outstanding**

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches
        the DB unescaped. (Also, the spec says prepared statements are required.)'
isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE
```

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: citation detection misses `#L61`-style line anchors (AC4) and accepts any URL**

Two asymmetric gaps in `CITATION_RES`, both verified against the shipped regexes:

1. **False negative — cited claims lose BLOCKING force (violates AC4).** GitHub-permalink style citations, the most common form in review threads, are not recognized:

   ```
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation from the reference (Policy.java#L61)') === false
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation (Policy.java:61-66)')                 === true
   ```

   A leg that did read the source and cited `Policy.java#L61` gets its verified finding demoted — precisely the strictness cut AC4 says this must not be.

2. **False positive — any URL counts as a citation.** `https?:\/\/[^\s)<>\]]+` matches *any* link, so "the spec says X is forbidden (see https://example.com/anything)" keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force with zero source verification. The leg can satisfy the guard by pasting an unrelated URL.

Suggested fix: add an anchor alternative to the file pattern — e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]+\.(?:java|…|md)#[LA]?\d+` — and, if feasible, restrict the URL arm to the actual source hosts the deployment trusts (or at least require the URL to sit on the same line as the spec-claim phrase).

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: two inline comments referencing the same file double-count the downgrade**

When two `inlineComments` entries point at the same `comment` file, each pass through the loop pushes its own rewrite and increments `downgrades` — verified:

```
same file twice: downgrades=2 rewrites=2 blocking=0 important=2
```

Consequences: `issueCounts.blocking` is decremented twice and `important` incremented twice for one physical comment, and the second `writeFile` silently overwrites the first (harmless here since both bodies carry the note, but the census drift is real and the machine cross-checks the census).

Consider memoizing by `c.comment` (first demotion wins, subsequent same-file entries get severity demoted without an extra census move), or grouping rewrites by path before returning.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: note says "confirm against the cited source" — but the whole point is there is no citation**

`DOWNGRADE_NOTE` ends with: *"Please confirm against the cited source; if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation and it regains blocking force."*

"the cited source" reads as if a citation exists; the demotion happened precisely because none did. Rephrase to reference what the finding actually named, e.g.: *"Please confirm against the source the finding references ('<source>'); if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation (file:line / doc URL) and it regains blocking force."* — ideally interpolating the spec-claim phrase that matched so the author knows exactly what to verify.

## PR Description

Closes #1053
### Root Cause
- Review prompts had no evidence rule for external-spec claims, so legs asserted "the spec/reference says X" at 🚨 BLOCKING without reading the source (live: a false exemption-list claim held a validated PR hostage).
- Machine-side, `postPRReviewComments.js` relayed such findings verbatim into threads, census, and the verdict record — one uncited claim could arm rework.

# gh-1053: Review legs must not post BLOCKING findings built on unverifiable external-spec claims

## Description

## Problem

AI review legs post **BLOCKING review threads whose core claim is "the external spec/reference says X" — without reading that reference**. The claim is unfalsifiable inside the leg, and when it is wrong the machine treats the thread as real rework demand: rework arms, legs dispatch, a green PR is held hostage until a human disproves the claim.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, dmtools-dart PR #423)

Review leg posted a 🚨 BLOCKING thread claiming "the spec (ticket, Java `JsEnvPolicy`) exempts only `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT`". The claim was false — Java uses contains-based exemptions (`JsEnvPolicy.java:61-66`), and the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it. Cost: a rework arm on a validated PR, two leg dispatches, human intervention.

Note: the Java-parity specifics of that case live in the dmtools-dart project — THIS issue is only about the general discipline, which applies to every deployment of this pack.

## Root cause

The review prompt has no rule about evidence for external-spec claims. A model without access to the referenced source fills the gap with plausible-sounding "the spec says" assertions — at BLOCKING severity, which the SM machinery then treats as ground truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review agents never assert "spec/reference/tool X does/does not Y" as a BLOCKING finding unless the finding quotes the exact source (file:line / doc URL) the leg actually read during the run.
- [ ] A spec-claim finding without a verifiable citation is downgraded to a non-blocking question ("please confirm against <source>").
- [ ] Unit test: review output containing an external-spec claim without a citation is classified non-blocking.
- [ ] Verified findings with citations keep full BLOCKING force — this is not a strictness cut.

## Non-goals

- Project-specific reference setups (e.g. Java-source verification for the dmtools-dart port) — those belong to the consuming project.

## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CI `crap` quality gate is red — 3 new functions over `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8`**

The unit suite is green (reproduced locally: 4333 passed / 0 failed, matching the PR description), but the failed `crap` check is the CRAP ratchet, and the job log (fetched via `gh run view 39154646821 --log-failed`) shows:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js::sanitizeReviewData: 23
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::loadWithFileMap: 23.4
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::file_read#10: 8.7
0 regression(s), 3 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

`classifyFindingSeverity` (CC 23, fully covered → CRAP 23) exceeds the threshold on complexity alone: the ratchet only admits new functions with CRAP ≤ 8, so no coverage percentage can save a CC > 8 function. Please split it — e.g. extract per-comment resolution (`body`/`comment` + `readText`), per-comment demotion application, and census/verdict rebalancing into separate ≤ 8-CC helpers.

The test side needs slimming too: `loadWithFileMap` (CC 23.4) duplicates the entire require-map construction — extract a shared `requireMap()` helper used by both it and the existing loaders, and collapse the nested `file_read` factories (the CC 8.7 `file_read#10`) into one small resolver function reused at both call sites.

Note for verification: `nyc instrument` + `crap4js --baseline` reproduces the verdict locally (install `github:IstiN/crap4js#83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` + `nyc@17` as in `.github/workflows/quality.yml`).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: incidental spec mentions demote genuine BLOCKING bugs — verdict can collapse to APPROVE with a real defect outstanding**

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches
        the DB unescaped. (Also, the spec says prepared statements are required.)'
isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE
```

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: citation detection misses `#L61`-style line anchors (AC4) and accepts any URL**

Two asymmetric gaps in `CITATION_RES`, both verified against the shipped regexes:

1. **False negative — cited claims lose BLOCKING force (violates AC4).** GitHub-permalink style citations, the most common form in review threads, are not recognized:

   ```
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation from the reference (Policy.java#L61)') === false
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation (Policy.java:61-66)')                 === true
   ```

   A leg that did read the source and cited `Policy.java#L61` gets its verified finding demoted — precisely the strictness cut AC4 says this must not be.

2. **False positive — any URL counts as a citation.** `https?:\/\/[^\s)<>\]]+` matches *any* link, so "the spec says X is forbidden (see https://example.com/anything)" keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force with zero source verification. The leg can satisfy the guard by pasting an unrelated URL.

Suggested fix: add an anchor alternative to the file pattern — e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]+\.(?:java|…|md)#[LA]?\d+` — and, if feasible, restrict the URL arm to the actual source hosts the deployment trusts (or at least require the URL to sit on the same line as the spec-claim phrase).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: two inline comments referencing the same file double-count the downgrade**

When two `inlineComments` entries point at the same `comment` file, each pass through the loop pushes its own rewrite and increments `downgrades` — verified:

```
same file twice: downgrades=2 rewrites=2 blocking=0 important=2
```

Consequences: `issueCounts.blocking` is decremented twice and `important` incremented twice for one physical comment, and the second `writeFile` silently overwrites the first (harmless here since both bodies carry the note, but the census drift is real and the machine cross-checks the census).

Consider memoizing by `c.comment` (first demotion wins, subsequent same-file entries get severity demoted without an extra census move), or grouping rewrites by path before returning.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: note says "confirm against the cited source" — but the whole point is there is no citation**

`DOWNGRADE_NOTE` ends with: *"Please confirm against the cited source; if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation and it regains blocking force."*

"the cited source" reads as if a citation exists; the demotion happened precisely because none did. Rephrase to reference what the finding actually named, e.g.: *"Please confirm against the source the finding references ('<source>'); if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation (file:line / doc URL) and it regains blocking force."* — ideally interpolating the spec-claim phrase that matched so the author knows exactly what to verify.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: misaligned indentation on the added require mappings**

The added `'./common/reviewSpecClaims.js'` lines are indented deeper than their sibling keys in the require map (e.g. here, and repeated at lines ~375, ~669, ~978, ~1358, ~2139, ~2472):

```javascript

                './common/reviewSpecClaims.js': loadModule('js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js', makeRequire({}), {})
```

# gh-1053: Review legs must not post BLOCKING findings built on unverifiable external-spec claims

## Description

## Problem

AI review legs post **BLOCKING review threads whose core claim is "the external spec/reference says X" — without reading that reference**. The claim is unfalsifiable inside the leg, and when it is wrong the machine treats the thread as real rework demand: rework arms, legs dispatch, a green PR is held hostage until a human disproves the claim.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, dmtools-dart PR #423)

Review leg posted a 🚨 BLOCKING thread claiming "the spec (ticket, Java `JsEnvPolicy`) exempts only `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT`". The claim was false — Java uses contains-based exemptions (`JsEnvPolicy.java:61-66`), and the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it. Cost: a rework arm on a validated PR, two leg dispatches, human intervention.

Note: the Java-parity specifics of that case live in the dmtools-dart project — THIS issue is only about the general discipline, which applies to every deployment of this pack.

## Root cause

The review prompt has no rule about evidence for external-spec claims. A model without access to the referenced source fills the gap with plausible-sounding "the spec says" assertions — at BLOCKING severity, which the SM machinery then treats as ground truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review agents never assert "spec/reference/tool X does/does not Y" as a BLOCKING finding unless the finding quotes the exact source (file:line / doc URL) the leg actually read during the run.
- [ ] A spec-claim finding without a verifiable citation is downgraded to a non-blocking question ("please confirm against <source>").
- [ ] Unit test: review output containing an external-spec claim without a citation is classified non-blocking.
- [ ] Verified findings with citations keep full BLOCKING force — this is not a strictness cut.

## Non-goals

- Project-specific reference setups (e.g. Java-source verification for the dmtools-dart port) — those belong to the consuming project.

## Machine jobs

- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39154691802) · started 18:34 · done 18:42 ✅
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-rework) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39155457257) · started 18:44 · done 18:47 🚫

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CI `crap` quality gate is red — 3 new functions over `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8`**

The unit suite is green (reproduced locally: 4333 passed / 0 failed, matching the PR description), but the failed `crap` check is the CRAP ratchet, and the job log (fetched via `gh run view 39154646821 --log-failed`) shows:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js::sanitizeReviewData: 23
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::loadWithFileMap: 23.4
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::file_read#10: 8.7

```

`classifyFindingSeverity` (CC 23, fully covered → CRAP 23) exceeds the threshold on complexity alone: the ratchet only admits new functions with CRAP ≤ 8, so no coverage percentage can save a CC > 8 function. Please split it — e.g. extract per-comment resolution (`body`/`comment` + `readText`), per-comment demotion application, and census/verdict rebalancing into separate ≤ 8-CC helpers.

The test side needs slimming too: `loadWithFileMap` (CC 23.4) duplicates the entire require-map construction — extract a shared `requireMap()` helper used by both it and the existing loaders, and collapse the nested `file_read` factories (the CC 8.7 `file_read#10`) into one small resolver function reused at both call sites.

Note for verification: `nyc instrument` + `crap4js --baseline` reproduces the verdict locally (install `github:IstiN/crap4js#83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` + `nyc@17` as in `.github/workflows/quality.yml`).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: incidental spec mentions demote genuine BLOCKING bugs — verdict can collapse to APPROVE with a real defect outstanding**

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches
        the DB unescaped. (Also, the spec says prepared statements are required.)'
isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE
```

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: citation detection misses `#L61`-style line anchors (AC4) and accepts any URL**

Two asymmetric gaps in `CITATION_RES`, both verified against the shipped regexes:

1. **False negative — cited claims lose BLOCKING force (violates AC4).** GitHub-permalink style citations, the most common form in review threads, are not recognized:

   ```
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation from the reference (Policy.java#L61)') === false
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation (Policy.java:61-66)')                 === true
   ```

   A leg that did read the source and cited `Policy.java#L61` gets its verified finding demoted — precisely the strictness cut AC4 says this must not be.

2. **False positive — any URL counts as a citation.** `https?:\/\/[^\s)<>\]]+` matches *any* link, so "the spec says X is forbidden (see https://example.com/anything)" keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force with zero source verification. The leg can satisfy the guard by pasting an unrelated URL.

Suggested fix: add an anchor alternative to the file pattern — e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]+\.(?:java|…|md)#[LA]?\d+` — and, if feasible, restrict the URL arm to the actual source hosts the deployment trusts (or at least require the URL to sit on the same line as the spec-claim phrase).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: two inline comments referencing the same file double-count the downgrade**

When two `inlineComments` entries point at the same `comment` file, each pass through the loop pushes its own rewrite and increments `downgrades` — verified:

```
same file twice: downgrades=2 rewrites=2 blocking=0 important=2
```

Consequences: `issueCounts.blocking` is decremented twice and `important` incremented twice for one physical comment, and the second `writeFile` silently overwrites the first (harmless here since both bodies carry the note, but the census drift is real and the machine cross-checks the census).

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

"the cited source" reads as if a citation exists; the demotion happened precisely because none did. ## PR Description

Closes #1053
### Root Cause
- Review prompts had no evidence rule for external-spec claims, so legs asserted "the spec/reference says X" at 🚨 BLOCKING without reading the source (live: a false exemption-list claim held a validated PR hostage).
- Machine-side, `postPRReviewComments.js` relayed such findings verbatim into threads, census, and the verdict record — one uncited claim could arm rework.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js` (new, pure): detects external-spec claims, verifiable citations (`file:line` / doc URL), classifies effective severity — uncited spec claim → non-blocking; cited claims keep full BLOCKING force.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: `applySpecClaimDowngrades` sanitizes `pr_review.json` before any verdict/census/posting — rewrites 🚨→⚠ bodies with a "confirm against source" note, rebalances `issueCounts`, collapses `REQUEST_CHANGES`→`APPROVE` when no cited blocker remains.
- `instructions/pr_review/general_guidelines.md`: new "External-spec evidence rule (gh-1053)"; `review_verdict_rules.md`: matching anti-pattern.

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewSpecClaims.js` — 18 tests: uncited spec claim → non-blocking (AC2/AC3), cited claim stays BLOCKING (AC4), non-spec findings untouched, census/verdict rebalancing. PASSED.
- `test_postPRReviewComments.js` — 2 wiring tests for `applySpecClaimDowngrades`. PASSED (93/93 in suite).
- Full suite: 4333 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- Downgrade target is IMPORTANT (non-blocking), phrased as a confirm-against-source question per AC2; the note invites re-raising as BLOCKING with a citation.
- Review test suites loading `postPRReviewComments.js` gained the new require mapping in their harnesses.

# gh-1053: Review legs must not post BLOCKING findings built on unverifiable external-spec claims

## Description

## Problem

AI review legs post **BLOCKING review threads whose core claim is "the external spec/reference says X" — without reading that reference**. The claim is unfalsifiable inside the leg, and when it is wrong the machine treats the thread as real rework demand: rework arms, legs dispatch, a green PR is held hostage until a human disproves the claim.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, dmtools-dart PR #423)

Review leg posted a 🚨 BLOCKING thread claiming "the spec (ticket, Java `JsEnvPolicy`) exempts only `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT`". The claim was false — Java uses contains-based exemptions (`JsEnvPolicy.java:61-66`), and the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it. Cost: a rework arm on a validated PR, two leg dispatches, human intervention.

Note: the Java-parity specifics of that case live in the dmtools-dart project — THIS issue is only about the general discipline, which applies to every deployment of this pack.

## Root cause

The review prompt has no rule about evidence for external-spec claims. A model without access to the referenced source fills the gap with plausible-sounding "the spec says" assertions — at BLOCKING severity, which the SM machinery then treats as ground truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review agents never assert "spec/reference/tool X does/does not Y" as a BLOCKING finding unless the finding quotes the exact source (file:line / doc URL) the leg actually read during the run.
- [ ] A spec-claim finding without a verifiable citation is downgraded to a non-blocking question ("please confirm against <source>").
- [ ] Unit test: review output containing an external-spec claim without a citation is classified non-blocking.
- [ ] Verified findings with citations keep full BLOCKING force — this is not a strictness cut.

## Non-goals

- Project-specific reference setups (e.g. Java-source verification for the dmtools-dart port) — those belong to the consuming project.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39153304741) · started 18:15 · done 18:33 ✅
- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39154691802) · started 18:34 · done 18:42 ✅
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-rework) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39155457257) · started 18:44 · done 18:47 🚫

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CI `crap` quality gate is red — 3 new functions over `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8`**

The unit suite is green (reproduced locally: 4333 passed / 0 failed, matching the PR description), but the failed `crap` check is the CRAP ratchet, and the job log (fetched via `gh run view 39154646821 --log-failed`) shows:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js::sanitizeReviewData: 23
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::loadWithFileMap: 23.4
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::file_read#10: 8.7
0 regression(s), 3 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

`classifyFindingSeverity` (CC 23, fully covered → CRAP 23) exceeds the threshold on complexity alone: the ratchet only admits new functions with CRAP ≤ 8, so no coverage percentage can save a CC > 8 function. Please split it — e.g. extract per-comment resolution (`body`/`comment` + `readText`), per-comment demotion application, and census/verdict rebalancing into separate ≤ 8-CC helpers.

The test side needs slimming too: `loadWithFileMap` (CC 23.4) duplicates the entire require-map construction — extract a shared `requireMap()` helper used by both it and the existing loaders, and collapse the nested `file_read` factories (the CC 8.7 `file_read#10`) into one small resolver function reused at both call sites.

Note for verification: `nyc instrument` + `crap4js --baseline` reproduces the verdict locally (install `github:IstiN/crap4js#83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` + `nyc@17` as in `.github/workflows/quality.yml`).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: incidental spec mentions demote genuine BLOCKING bugs — verdict can collapse to APPROVE with a real defect outstanding**

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches
        the DB unescaped. (Also, the spec says prepared statements are required.)'
isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE
```

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: citation detection misses `#L61`-style line anchors (AC4) and accepts any URL**

Two asymmetric gaps in `CITATION_RES`, both verified against the shipped regexes:

1. **False negative — cited claims lose BLOCKING force (violates AC4).** GitHub-permalink style citations, the most common form in review threads, are not recognized:

   ```
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation from the reference (Policy.java#L61)') === false
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation (Policy.java:61-66)')                 === true
   ```

   A leg that did read the source and cited `Policy.java#L61` gets its verified finding demoted — precisely the strictness cut AC4 says this must not be.

2. **False positive — any URL counts as a citation.** `https?:\/\/[^\s)<>\]]+` matches *any* link, so "the spec says X is forbidden (see https://example.com/anything)" keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force with zero source verification. The leg can satisfy the guard by pasting an unrelated URL.

Suggested fix: add an anchor alternative to the file pattern — e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]+\.(?:java|…|md)#[LA]?\d+` — and, if feasible, restrict the URL arm to the actual source hosts the deployment trusts (or at least require the URL to sit on the same line as the spec-claim phrase).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: two inline comments referencing the same file double-count the downgrade**

When two `inlineComments` entries point at the same `comment` file, each pass through the loop pushes its own rewrite and increments `downgrades` — verified:

```
same file twice: downgrades=2 rewrites=2 blocking=0 important=2

## PR Description

Closes #1053
### Root Cause
- Review prompts had no evidence rule for external-spec claims, so legs asserted "the spec/reference says X" at 🚨 BLOCKING without reading the source (live: a false exemption-list claim held a validated PR hostage).
- Machine-side, `postPRReviewComments.js` relayed such findings verbatim into threads, census, and the verdict record — one uncited claim could arm rework.

# gh-1053: Review legs must not post BLOCKING findings built on unverifiable external-spec claims

## Description

## Problem

AI review legs post **BLOCKING review threads whose core claim is "the external spec/reference says X" — without reading that reference**. The claim is unfalsifiable inside the leg, and when it is wrong the machine treats the thread as real rework demand: rework arms, legs dispatch, a green PR is held hostage until a human disproves the claim.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, dmtools-dart PR #423)

Review leg posted a 🚨 BLOCKING thread claiming "the spec (ticket, Java `JsEnvPolicy`) exempts only `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT`". The claim was false — Java uses contains-based exemptions (`JsEnvPolicy.java:61-66`), and the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it. Cost: a rework arm on a validated PR, two leg dispatches, human intervention.

Note: the Java-parity specifics of that case live in the dmtools-dart project — THIS issue is only about the general discipline, which applies to every deployment of this pack.

## Root cause

The review prompt has no rule about evidence for external-spec claims. A model without access to the referenced source fills the gap with plausible-sounding "the spec says" assertions — at BLOCKING severity, which the SM machinery then treats as ground truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review agents never assert "spec/reference/tool X does/does not Y" as a BLOCKING finding unless the finding quotes the exact source (file:line / doc URL) the leg actually read during the run.
- [ ] A spec-claim finding without a verifiable citation is downgraded to a non-blocking question ("please confirm against <source>").
- [ ] Unit test: review output containing an external-spec claim without a citation is classified non-blocking.
- [ ] Verified findings with citations keep full BLOCKING force — this is not a strictness cut.

## Non-goals

- Project-specific reference setups (e.g. Java-source verification for the dmtools-dart port) — those belong to the consuming project.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CI `crap` quality gate is red — 3 new functions over `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8`**

The unit suite is green (reproduced locally: 4333 passed / 0 failed, matching the PR description), but the failed `crap` check is the CRAP ratchet, and the job log (fetched via `gh run view 39154646821 --log-failed`) shows:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js::sanitizeReviewData: 23
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::loadWithFileMap: 23.4
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::file_read#10: 8.7
0 regression(s), 3 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

`classifyFindingSeverity` (CC 23, fully covered → CRAP 23) exceeds the threshold on complexity alone: the ratchet only admits new functions with CRAP ≤ 8, so no coverage percentage can save a CC > 8 function. Please split it — e.g. extract per-comment resolution (`body`/`comment` + `readText`), per-comment demotion application, and census/verdict rebalancing into separate ≤ 8-CC helpers.

The test side needs slimming too: `loadWithFileMap` (CC 23.4) duplicates the entire require-map construction — extract a shared `requireMap()` helper used by both it and the existing loaders, and collapse the nested `file_read` factories (the CC 8.7 `file_read#10`) into one small resolver function reused at both call sites.

Note for verification: `nyc instrument` + `crap4js --baseline` reproduces the verdict locally (install `github:IstiN/crap4js#83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` + `nyc@17` as in `.github/workflows/quality.yml`).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: incidental spec mentions demote genuine BLOCKING bugs — verdict can collapse to APPROVE with a real defect outstanding**

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches
        the DB unescaped. (Also, the spec says prepared statements are required.)'
isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE
```

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: citation detection misses `#L61`-style line anchors (AC4) and accepts any URL**

Two asymmetric gaps in `CITATION_RES`, both verified against the shipped regexes:

1. **False negative — cited claims lose BLOCKING force (violates AC4).** GitHub-permalink style citations, the most common form in review threads, are not recognized:

   ```
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation from the reference (Policy.java#L61)') === false
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation (Policy.java:61-66)')                 === true
   ```

   A leg that did read the source and cited `Policy.java#L61` gets its verified finding demoted — precisely the strictness cut AC4 says this must not be.

2. **False positive — any URL counts as a citation.** `https?:\/\/[^\s)<>\]]+` matches *any* link, so "the spec says X is forbidden (see https://example.com/anything)" keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force with zero source verification. The leg can satisfy the guard by pasting an unrelated URL.

Suggested fix: add an anchor alternative to the file pattern — e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]+\.(?:java|…|md)#[LA]?\d+` — and, if feasible, restrict the URL arm to the actual source hosts the deployment trusts (or at least require the URL to sit on the same line as the spec-claim phrase).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: two inline comments referencing the same file double-count the downgrade**

When two `inlineComments` entries point at the same `comment` file, each pass through the loop pushes its own rewrite and increments `downgrades` — verified:

```
same file twice: downgrades=2 rewrites=2 blocking=0 important=2
```

Consequences: `issueCounts.blocking` is decremented twice and `important` incremented twice for one physical comment, and the second `writeFile` silently overwrites the first (harmless here since both bodies carry the note, but the census drift is real and the machine cross-checks the census).

Consider memoizing by `c.comment` (first demotion wins, subsequent same-file entries get severity demoted without an extra census move), or grouping rewrites by path before returning.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: note says "confirm against the cited source" — but the whole point is there is no citation**

`DOWNGRADE_NOTE` ends with: *"Please confirm against the cited source; if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation and it regains blocking force."*

"the cited source" reads as if a citation exists; the demotion happened precisely because none did. Rephrase to reference what the finding actually named, e.g.: *"Please confirm against the source the finding references ('<source>'); if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation (file:line / doc URL) and it regains blocking force."* — ideally interpolating the spec-claim phrase that matched so the author knows exactly what to verify.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: misaligned indentation on the added require mappings**

The added `'./common/reviewSpecClaims.js'` lines are indented deeper than their sibling keys in the require map (e.g. here, and repeated at lines ~375, ~669, ~978, ~1358, ~2139, ~2472):

Closes #1053
### Root Cause
- Review prompts had no evidence rule for external-spec claims, so legs asserted "the spec/reference says X" at 🚨 BLOCKING without reading the source (live: a false exemption-list claim held a validated PR hostage).

- `test_reviewSpecClaims.js` — 18 tests: uncited spec claim → non-blocking (AC2/AC3), cited claim stays BLOCKING (AC4), non-spec findings untouched, census/verdict rebalancing. PASSED.
- `test_postPRReviewComments.js` — 2 wiring tests for `applySpecClaimDowngrades`. PASSED (93/93 in suite).
- Full suite: 4333 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- Downgrade target is IMPORTANT (non-blocking), phrased as a confirm-against-source question per AC2; the note invites re-raising as BLOCKING with a citation.
- Review test suites loading `postPRReviewComments.js` gained the new require mapping in their harnesses.

# gh-1053: Review legs must not post BLOCKING findings built on unverifiable external-spec claims

## Description

## Problem

AI review legs post **BLOCKING review threads whose core claim is "the external spec/reference says X" — without reading that reference**. The claim is unfalsifiable inside the leg, and when it is wrong the machine treats the thread as real rework demand: rework arms, legs dispatch, a green PR is held hostage until a human disproves the claim.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, dmtools-dart PR #423)

Review leg posted a 🚨 BLOCKING thread claiming "the spec (ticket, Java `JsEnvPolicy`) exempts only `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT`". The claim was false — Java uses contains-based exemptions (`JsEnvPolicy.java:61-66`), and the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it. Cost: a rework arm on a validated PR, two leg dispatches, human intervention.

Note: the Java-parity specifics of that case live in the dmtools-dart project — THIS issue is only about the general discipline, which applies to every deployment of this pack.

## Root cause

The review prompt has no rule about evidence for external-spec claims. A model without access to the referenced source fills the gap with plausible-sounding "the spec says" assertions — at BLOCKING severity, which the SM machinery then treats as ground truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review agents never assert "spec/reference/tool X does/does not Y" as a BLOCKING finding unless the finding quotes the exact source (file:line / doc URL) the leg actually read during the run.
- [ ] A spec-claim finding without a verifiable citation is downgraded to a non-blocking question ("please confirm against <source>").
- [ ] Unit test: review output containing an external-spec claim without a citation is classified non-blocking.
- [ ] Verified findings with citations keep full BLOCKING force — this is not a strictness cut.

## Non-goals

- Project-specific reference setups (e.g. Java-source verification for the dmtools-dart port) — those belong to the consuming project.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39153304741) · started 18:15 · done 18:33 ✅
- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39154691802) · started 18:34 · done 18:42 ✅
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-rework) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39155457257) · started 18:44 · done 18:47 🚫

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CI `crap` quality gate is red — 3 new functions over `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8`**

The unit suite is green (reproduced locally: 4333 passed / 0 failed, matching the PR description), but the failed `crap` check is the CRAP ratchet, and the job log (fetched via `gh run view 39154646821 --log-failed`) shows:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js::sanitizeReviewData: 23
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::loadWithFileMap: 23.4
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::file_read#10: 8.7
0 regression(s), 3 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

`classifyFindingSeverity` (CC 23, fully covered → CRAP 23) exceeds the threshold on complexity alone: the ratchet only admits new functions with CRAP ≤ 8, so no coverage percentage can save a CC > 8 function. Please split it — e.g. extract per-comment resolution (`body`/`comment` + `readText`), per-comment demotion application, and census/verdict rebalancing into separate ≤ 8-CC helpers.

The test side needs slimming too: `loadWithFileMap` (CC 23.4) duplicates the entire require-map construction — extract a shared `requireMap()` helper used by both it and the existing loaders, and collapse the nested `file_read` factories (the CC 8.7 `file_read#10`) into one small resolver function reused at both call sites.

Note for verification: `nyc instrument` + `crap4js --baseline` reproduces the verdict locally (install `github:IstiN/crap4js#83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` + `nyc@17` as in `.github/workflows/quality.yml`).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: incidental spec mentions demote genuine BLOCKING bugs — verdict can collapse to APPROVE with a real defect outstanding**

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches
        the DB unescaped. (Also, the spec says prepared statements are required.)'
isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE
```

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: citation detection misses `#L61`-style line anchors (AC4) and accepts any URL**

Two asymmetric gaps in `CITATION_RES`, both verified against the shipped regexes:

1. **False negative — cited claims lose BLOCKING force (violates AC4).** GitHub-permalink style citations, the most common form in review threads, are not recognized:

   ```
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation from the reference (Policy.java#L61)') === false
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation (Policy.java:61-66)')                 === true
   ```

   A leg that did read the source and cited `Policy.java#L61` gets its verified finding demoted — precisely the strictness cut AC4 says this must not be.

2. **False positive — any URL counts as a citation.** `https?:\/\/[^\s)<>\]]+` matches *any* link, so "the spec says X is forbidden (see https://example.com/anything)" keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force with zero source verification. The leg can satisfy the guard by pasting an unrelated URL.

Suggested fix: add an anchor alternative to the file pattern — e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]+\.(?:java|…|md)#[LA]?\d+` — and, if feasible, restrict the URL arm to the actual source hosts the deployment trusts (or at least require the URL to sit on the same line as the spec-claim phrase).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: two inline comments referencing the same file double-count the downgrade**

When two `inlineComments` entries point at the same `comment` file, each pass through the loop pushes its own rewrite and increments `downgrades` — verified:

```
same file twice: downgrades=2 rewrites=2 blocking=0 important=2
```

Consequences: `issueCounts.blocking` is decremented twice and `important` incremented twice for one physical comment, and the second `writeFile` silently overwrites the first (harmless here since both bodies carry the note, but the census drift is real and the machine cross-checks the census).

Consider memoizing by `c.comment` (first demotion wins, subsequent same-file entries get severity demoted without an extra census move), or grouping rewrites by path before returning.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: note says "confirm against the cited source" — but the whole point is there is no citation**

`DOWNGRADE_NOTE` ends with: *"Please confirm against the cited source; if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation and it regains blocking force."*

"the cited source" reads as if a citation exists; the demotion happened precisely because none did. Rephrase to reference what the finding actually named, e.g.: *"Please confirm against the source the finding references ('<source>'); if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation (file:line / doc URL) and it regains blocking force."* — ideally interpolating the spec-claim phrase that matched so the author knows exactly what to verify.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: misaligned indentation on the added require mappings**

The added `'./common/reviewSpecClaims.js'` lines are indented deeper than their sibling keys in the require map (e.g. here, and repeated at lines ~375, ~669, ~978, ~1358, ~2139, ~2472):

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # gh-1053: Review legs must not post BLOCKING findings built on unverifiable external-spec claims

## Description

## Problem

AI review legs post **BLOCKING review threads whose core claim is "the external spec/reference says X" — without reading that reference**. The claim is unfalsifiable inside the leg, and when it is wrong the machine treats the thread as real rework demand: rework arms, legs dispatch, a green PR is held hostage until a human disproves the claim.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, dmtools-dart PR #423)

Review leg posted a 🚨 BLOCKING thread claiming "the spec (ticket, Java `JsEnvPolicy`) exempts only `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT`". The claim was false — Java uses contains-based exemptions (`JsEnvPolicy.java:61-66`), and the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it. Cost: a rework arm on a validated PR, two leg dispatches, human intervention.

Note: the Java-parity specifics of that case live in the dmtools-dart project — THIS issue is only about the general discipline, which applies to every deployment of this pack.

## Root cause

The review prompt has no rule about evidence for external-spec claims. A model without access to the referenced source fills the gap with plausible-sounding "the spec says" assertions — at BLOCKING severity, which the SM machinery then treats as ground truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review agents never assert "spec/reference/tool X does/does not Y" as a BLOCKING finding unless the finding quotes the exact source (file:line / doc URL) the leg actually read during the run.
- [ ] A spec-claim finding without a verifiable citation is downgraded to a non-blocking question ("please confirm against <source>").
- [ ] Unit test: review output containing an external-spec claim without a citation is classified non-blocking.
- [ ] Verified findings with citations keep full BLOCKING force — this is not a strictness cut.

## Non-goals

- Project-specific reference setups (e.g. Java-source verification for the dmtools-dart port) — those belong to the consuming project.

## Machine jobs

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches

isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.

## PR Description

Closes #1053
### Root Cause
- Review prompts had no evidence rule for external-spec claims, so legs asserted "the spec/reference says X" at 🚨 BLOCKING without reading the source (live: a false exemption-list claim held a validated PR hostage).

- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: `applySpecClaimDowngrades` sanitizes `pr_review.json` before any verdict/census/posting — rewrites 🚨→⚠ bodies with a "confirm against source" note, rebalances `issueCounts`, collapses `REQUEST_CHANGES`→`APPROVE` when no cited blocker remains.

- `test_reviewSpecClaims.js` — 18 tests: uncited spec claim → non-blocking (AC2/AC3), cited claim stays BLOCKING (AC4), non-spec findings untouched, census/verdict rebalancing. PASSED.
- `test_postPRReviewComments.js` — 2 wiring tests for `applySpecClaimDowngrades`. PASSED (93/93 in suite).
- Full suite: 4333 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- Downgrade target is IMPORTANT (non-blocking), phrased as a confirm-against-source question per AC2; the note invites re-raising as BLOCKING with a citation.
- Review test suites loading `postPRReviewComments.js` gained the new require mapping in their harnesses.

# gh-1053: Review legs must not post BLOCKING findings built on unverifiable external-spec claims

## Description

## Problem

AI review legs post **BLOCKING review threads whose core claim is "the external spec/reference says X" — without reading that reference**. The claim is unfalsifiable inside the leg, and when it is wrong the machine treats the thread as real rework demand: rework arms, legs dispatch, a green PR is held hostage until a human disproves the claim.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, dmtools-dart PR #423)

Review leg posted a 🚨 BLOCKING thread claiming "the spec (ticket, Java `JsEnvPolicy`) exempts only `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT`". The claim was false — Java uses contains-based exemptions (`JsEnvPolicy.java:61-66`), and the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it. Cost: a rework arm on a validated PR, two leg dispatches, human intervention.

Note: the Java-parity specifics of that case live in the dmtools-dart project — THIS issue is only about the general discipline, which applies to every deployment of this pack.

## Root cause

The review prompt has no rule about evidence for external-spec claims. A model without access to the referenced source fills the gap with plausible-sounding "the spec says" assertions — at BLOCKING severity, which the SM machinery then treats as ground truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review agents never assert "spec/reference/tool X does/does not Y" as a BLOCKING finding unless the finding quotes the exact source (file:line / doc URL) the leg actually read during the run.
- [ ] A spec-claim finding without a verifiable citation is downgraded to a non-blocking question ("please confirm against <source>").
- [ ] Unit test: review output containing an external-spec claim without a citation is classified non-blocking.
- [ ] Verified findings with citations keep full BLOCKING force — this is not a strictness cut.

## Non-goals

- Project-specific reference setups (e.g. Java-source verification for the dmtools-dart port) — those belong to the consuming project.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39153304741) · started 18:15 · done 18:33 ✅

- [x] ▶ dev (fa-rework) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39155457257) · started 18:44 · done 18:47 🚫

## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CI `crap` quality gate is red — 3 new functions over `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8`**

The unit suite is green (reproduced locally: 4333 passed / 0 failed, matching the PR description), but the failed `crap` check is the CRAP ratchet, and the job log (fetched via `gh run view 39154646821 --log-failed`) shows:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js::sanitizeReviewData: 23
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::loadWithFileMap: 23.4
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::file_read#10: 8.7
0 regression(s), 3 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

`classifyFindingSeverity` (CC 23, fully covered → CRAP 23) exceeds the threshold on complexity alone: the ratchet only admits new functions with CRAP ≤ 8, so no coverage percentage can save a CC > 8 function. Please split it — e.g. extract per-comment resolution (`body`/`comment` + `readText`), per-comment demotion application, and census/verdict rebalancing into separate ≤ 8-CC helpers.

The test side needs slimming too: `loadWithFileMap` (CC 23.4) duplicates the entire require-map construction — extract a shared `requireMap()` helper used by both it and the existing loaders, and collapse the nested `file_read` factories (the CC 8.7 `file_read#10`) into one small resolver function reused at both call sites.

Note for verification: `nyc instrument` + `crap4js --baseline` reproduces the verdict locally (install `github:IstiN/crap4js#83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` + `nyc@17` as in `.github/workflows/quality.yml`).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: incidental spec mentions demote genuine BLOCKING bugs — verdict can collapse to APPROVE with a real defect outstanding**

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches
        the DB unescaped. (Also, the spec says prepared statements are required.)'
isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE
```

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: citation detection misses `#L61`-style line anchors (AC4) and accepts any URL**

Two asymmetric gaps in `CITATION_RES`, both verified against the shipped regexes:

1. **False negative — cited claims lose BLOCKING force (violates AC4).** GitHub-permalink style citations, the most common form in review threads, are not recognized:

   ```
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation from the reference (Policy.java#L61)') === false
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation (Policy.java:61-66)')                 === true
   ```

   A leg that did read the source and cited `Policy.java#L61` gets its verified finding demoted — precisely the strictness cut AC4 says this must not be.

2. **False positive — any URL counts as a citation.** `https?:\/\/[^\s)<>\]]+` matches *any* link, so "the spec says X is forbidden (see https://example.com/anything)" keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force with zero source verification. The leg can satisfy the guard by pasting an unrelated URL.

Suggested fix: add an anchor alternative to the file pattern — e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]+\.(?:java|…|md)#[LA]?\d+` — and, if feasible, restrict the URL arm to the actual source hosts the deployment trusts (or at least require the URL to sit on the same line as the spec-claim phrase).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: two inline comments referencing the same file double-count the downgrade**

When two `inlineComments` entries point at the same `comment` file, each pass through the loop pushes its own rewrite and increments `downgrades` — verified:

```
same file twice: downgrades=2 rewrites=2 blocking=0 important=2
```

Consequences: `issueCounts.blocking` is decremented twice and `important` incremented twice for one physical comment, and the second `writeFile` silently overwrites the first (harmless here since both bodies carry the note, but the census drift is real and the machine cross-checks the census).

Consider memoizing by `c.comment` (first demotion wins, subsequent same-file entries get severity demoted without an extra census move), or grouping rewrites by path before returning.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: note says "confirm against the cited source" — but the whole point is there is no citation**

`DOWNGRADE_NOTE` ends with: *"Please confirm against the cited source; if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation and it regains blocking force."*

"the cited source" reads as if a citation exists; the demotion happened precisely because none did. Rephrase to reference what the finding actually named, e.g.: *"Please confirm against the source the finding references ('<source>'); if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation (file:line / doc URL) and it regains blocking force."* — ideally interpolating the spec-claim phrase that matched so the author knows exactly what to verify.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: misaligned indentation on the added require mappings**

The added `'./common/reviewSpecClaims.js'` lines are indented deeper than their sibling keys in the require map (e.g. here, and repeated at lines ~375, ~669, ~978, ~1358, ~2139, ~2472):

```javascript

```

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
